note: Double solid yellow lines indicate no passing by traffic in either direction, except for turning or where necessary to avoid hazards.

question: Defensive drivers typically:
options: a:Anticipate what others might do and prepare to react.,b:Always assume no one will yield to them.,c:Expect other drivers to always do the right thing.
note: Defensive driving means predicting potential mistakes by others and being prepared to respond safely.

question: Temporary signs in construction and maintenance areas have what colors?
options: a:Yellow background with blue writing.,b:Red background with green writing.,c:Orange background with black writing.
note: Work zone signs are orange with black letters or symbols—use extra caution in these areas.

question: If another vehicle appears likely to hit you, you should:
options: a:Wave your arms.,b:Sound your horn to warn them.,c:Only use emergency lights.
note: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians if you believe they may not see you and a collision is imminent.

question: What general rule should you follow when driving in a construction zone?
options: a:Expect the unexpected and use extra caution.,b:Expect construction workers to yield to motorists.,c:Drive slightly faster to clear the zone quickly.
note: Construction zones often have unexpected conditions; reduce speed and drive with extraordinary caution for workers and other road users.

question: If your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Wait for police before moving the vehicle even if it creates a hazard.,b:Never move your vehicle under any circumstances.,c:Move your vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway.,d:Leave the vehicle and wait in the middle of the road.
note: After a minor collision, move vehicles off the roadway if possible; do not leave the scene without identifying yourself and assisting if needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The posted maximum speed limit is the fastest you may legally drive under ideal conditions:
options: a:False,b:True,c:
note: The posted maximum speed is the legal limit under ideal conditions; you must drive slower when conditions require it.

question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what is the correct action?
options: a:Drive slowly and pass them,b:Honk and proceed as normal.,c:Wait and let the pedestrians finish crossing.,d:Speed up to clear the crosswalk before they arrive.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk and wait until the intersection is clear before proceeding.

question: What does a yellow-and-black diamond-shaped sign indicate?
options: a:Services such as gas or food.,b:Traffic laws and regulations.,c:Warning about conditions on or near the road ahead.,d:Directions to nearby cities and towns.
note: Diamond-shaped yellow warning signs alert drivers to special conditions or hazards ahead.

question: How often should drivers check their mirrors for traffic behind them?
options: a:About every 45 seconds.,b:About every 20 seconds.,c:About every 10 seconds.
note: Check mirrors frequently—roughly every six to eight seconds—so 10 seconds is the closest choice provided.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is true about passing maneuvers?
options: a:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass and ensure there is no oncoming traffic.,b:Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing to the left.,c:When passing, wait until you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror before returning to your original lane.,d:All of the above.
note: When passing, signal well in advance, check mirrors and blind spots, and only return to your lane after you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your mirror.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Coordination only,b:Alertness only,c:Both coordination and alertness
note: Alcohol and drugs impair multiple driving skills including coordination, alertness, and reaction time.

question: An orange-colored road sign typically indicates:
options: a:The start of a no-passing zone.,b:Construction,c:A school zone is ahead.,d:A railroad crossing is ahead.
note: Orange signs warn of construction, maintenance, or emergency operations on or near the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers must always yield the right-of-way to pedestrians, even if the pedestrian ignores a traffic signal.
options: a:True,b:False
note: You are required to yield to pedestrians; they may misjudge signals and you must avoid a collision.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn continuously to get attention.,b:Pull off the road,c:Get out and flag down the first passing car.,d:Walk along the shoulder to find help immediately.
note: On interstates, remain in your vehicle if safe, use hazard lights, and avoid walking on the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should your vehicle end up?
options: a:In the left lane of the street you are entering.,b:In the right lane of the street.,c:In the center of the street.
note: When turning left onto a one-way street, complete the turn into the lane closest to the lane you came from — typically the left lane of the one-way street.

question: If you see one deer or moose cross the road, should you expect more?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Deer and moose often travel in groups; if one crosses, others may follow.

question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn they may:
options: a:Use the left lane or make a proper left-turn movement like a vehicle.,b:Cut through multiple lanes recklessly.,c:Always wait on the sidewalk.
note: Bicyclists may use the left lane to make left turns and should be expected to follow normal turning rules.

question: The best way to avoid hydroplaning in wet conditions is to:
options: a:Lower your speed.,b:Increase your speed to pass water quickly.,c:Use cruise control at a reduced speed.
note: Reducing speed in wet conditions decreases the chance your tires will ride on top of standing water (hydroplane).

question: Which of the following does not promote safer night driving?
options: a:Rely solely on a flashlight to improve road vision.,b:Be aware that tinted windows reduce visibility in the dark.,c:Keep your windshield clean.
note: Maintain a clean windshield and be aware that heavy tinting reduces night visibility; flashlights are not a substitute for proper lighting and driving techniques.

question: The most common mistake drivers make when backing is failing to look both ways behind them.
options: a:False,b:True
note: Mirrors alone do not provide a complete view; turn and look through the rear window to check while backing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, when should you return to your lane?
options: a:Remain in the left lane if you plan to turn left soon.,b:Stay in the left lane until the vehicle ahead signals you to move back.,c:Return to the right side of the roadway as soon as there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.
note: On a two-lane roadway, after passing another vehicle you must return to the right side when there is sufficient room between you and the passed vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Preparing to make a left turn from a two-way street, you should position your vehicle:
options: a:To the left of the centerline into opposing traffic.,b:Near the centerline,c:On the right-hand side of the road.
note: Begin left turns from the lane closest to the centerline; do not cut the corner or swing wide.

question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:Only in front of the vehicle.,b:Only in back of your vehicle.,c:Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.
note: You should maintain a cushion of space on all sides of your vehicle to allow time to react to hazards; do not crowd other vehicles.

question: If the roadway is wet or icy, what should you do?
options: a:Drive at the posted speed.,b:Speed up.,c:Reduce your speed.
note: Wet, snowy, or icy conditions reduce tire traction—slow down and increase your following distance.

question: Is it legal to consume alcoholic beverages in a vehicle on a public highway?
options: a:No,b:Yes,c:You yes
note: It is illegal to possess or consume an open alcoholic beverage in a motor vehicle on public roads, and open containers in the driver/passenger area are prohibited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a stopped school bus displaying its stop arm, drivers should:
options: a:Assume children are done and pass slowly.,b:Honk before passing on the left,c:Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
note: Drivers must stop for a school bus that is using its stop signal and remain stopped until the signal is withdrawn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are turning left onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Into the farthest lane from your prior lane.,b:Into the rightmost lane regardless of position.,c:Into any lane you choose as long as it's clear.,d:Into the lane closest to your previous lane (the nearest lane).
note: When turning left onto a one-way street, complete the turn into the lane closest to the lane you came from.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Expect oncoming traffic and pedestrians to yield to you.,b:Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,c:Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians in the roadway or crosswalk.

question: Signs that require drivers to obey an instruction are called what?
options: a:Warning signs.,b:Guide signs.,c:Regulatory signs.,d:Information signs.
note: Regulatory signs must be obeyed; failure to comply can result in penalties.

question: If your gas pedal becomes stuck, you should:
options: a:Turn off your headlights and continue driving.,b:Shift into neutral,c:Keep accelerating to escape danger.
note: Shift to neutral to cut engine power, apply brakes, steer safely off-road, then stop and turn off the engine; call for help if needed.

question: Excessive speed most often does what to driving behavior?
options: a:Does not increase the chance of a crash.,b:Increases your ability to react to a hazard.,c:Often leads to high-risk decision-making.
note: Driving at excessive speeds reduces reaction time and often encourages dangerous maneuvers that increase crash risk.

question: Which traffic signal indication requires you to come to a complete stop, yield, then proceed when clear?
options: a:A flashing red light.,b:A solid green light.,c:A flashing yellow light.
note: A flashing red signal means stop, yield to cross traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when it is safe, like a stop sign.

question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:
options: a:Overcorrect to regain control.,b:Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid.,c:Turn the wheel into oncoming traffic sharply.
note: If your vehicle skids, stay calm and steer in the same direction the rear of the vehicle is sliding to regain control.

question: When approaching railroad tracks, you should:
options: a:Speed up to cross quickly before any gates lower.,b:Look and listen,c:Creep across without stopping if clear.,d:Drive around lowered gates if no train is visible.
note: Approach tracks with caution; look and listen and stop if necessary for trains or other hazards.

question: If you experience a tire blowout while driving, what is the correct immediate action?
options: a:Keep driving normally.,b:Gradually slow down and pull off the roadway.,c:Slam on your brakes.
note: Take your foot off the gas, avoid heavy braking, slow gradually, and steer to a safe area off the road.

question: Is it wise to continually improve your driving and observation skills?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Driving skills should be constantly improved to reduce risk and stay safe on the road.

question: How should you check your blind spots when preparing to change lanes?
options: a:Rely only on the inside rearview mirror.,b:Rely only on the outside rearview mirror.,c:Use your horn instead of looking.,d:Turn your head to glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot.
note: Before every lane change, turn your head and look over your shoulder to ensure your blind spot is clear; don't rely solely on mirrors.

question: When you see a person crossing with a white cane or guide dog, you should:
options: a:Stop until the person is well clear of your path.,b:Honk to alert them.,c:Carefully drive around them while they cross.
note: Stop and wait until the pedestrian using a cane or guide dog has safely cleared your path; always yield to blind pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to make a left turn, which action is important?
options: a:Move into the left lane before reaching the intersection.,b:Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,c:Only use your rearview mirror to check behind you.
note: As you prepare for a left turn, signal, slow gradually, check mirrors, move into the left lane when appropriate, and yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a vehicle entering the interstate from an entrance ramp, what should you generally do?
options: a:Speed up to pass the merging vehicle.,b:Ignore them because you have the right-of-way.,c:Stop on the highway shoulder to let them in.,d:Make room by changing lanes or adjusting speed to allow them to merge.
note: Whenever possible, change lanes or slow slightly to allow vehicles to enter the interstate smoothly and safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to move back into your driving lane?
options: a:After signaling for three seconds.,b:When the driver you passed signals you to return.,c:Immediately after completing the pass regardless of distance.,d:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: You should only return to your lane when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your inside rearview mirror, indicating a safe distance.

question: Do large vehicles have blind spots extending far behind them?
options: a:Only buses have large blind spots.,b:Only when they are towing a trailer.,c:False — large vehicles have smaller blind spots than cars.,d:True — large vehicles can have blind spots extending up to 200 feet behind them.
note: Large vehicles can have extensive blind spots behind them; avoid tailgating because they may not see you.

question: What typically causes a vehicle to hydroplane?
options: a:Driving too fast for wet road conditions, causing tires to lose contact with the road.,b:Sudden braking on dry pavement.,c:Excessive stops during a trip.,d:A fully worn steering wheel.
note: Hydroplaning occurs when tires cannot clear water at higher speeds, causing the vehicle to slide on a film of water.

question: The best way to avoid hydroplaning is to:
options: a:Drive at normal highway speeds when roads are wet.,b:Drive over puddles quickly to reduce time on water.,c:Use cruise control on wet roads.,d:Keep tires properly maintained
note: Well-maintained tires and reduced speeds in wet conditions lessen hydroplaning risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you and the driver on your left arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Whoever is signaling to make a turn has the right-of-way.,b:You have the right-of-way.,c:The driver on your left has the right-of-way.
note: When two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way; if the other driver is on your left, you are to their right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic light displays a red light and a green arrow for the same direction, can you turn in the arrow's direction?
options: a:True,b:False,c:
note: If a green arrow is displayed, after yielding as required you may proceed in the direction of the arrow regardless of the steady red light.

question: You should avoid using your horn:
options: a:When visibility ahead is limited.,b:If you might collide with another vehicle.,c:Near blind pedestrians.
note: Sounding the horn near blind pedestrians can be dangerous; yield and proceed only when safe.

question: If you borrow an unfamiliar vehicle, what should you do before driving it?
options: a:Not put much thought into it because all vehicles are the same.,b:Disregard defects to avoid embarrassing your friend.,c:Familiarize yourself with the vehicle's controls and correct any obvious defects before driving.
note: Take time to locate and test signals, lights, wipers, brakes, gears, and the horn; correct defects before operating the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate highway, what should you do?
options: a:Always stop before entering the highway.,b:Select a safe gap and merge into the lane of traffic.,c:Merge across two lanes at once.
note: Pick a sufficiently large gap in traffic and merge smoothly into the main lane; do not stop on the entrance ramp unless absolutely necessary.

question: When parking facing uphill on a road with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the wheels away from the edge of the road (to the left).,b:Keep the wheels facing straight ahead.,c:Turn the wheels so they point uphill.,d:Turn the wheels toward the edge of the road (to the right).
note: When parking uphill with no curb, turn your wheels toward the right edge of the road so a roll will move the vehicle off the traveled way.

question: What is the safest way to drive through a curve?
options: a:Speed up as you enter and slow down as you exit.,b:Maintain a constant speed throughout the curve.,c:Slow down as you enter and increase speed as you exit.
note: Reduce speed before entering a curve and accelerate gradually as you exit to maintain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it true that drivers are not required to yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Drivers must stop and yield to pedestrians in marked crosswalks. You must also yield to pedestrians in unmarked crosswalks on your side of the roadway when there are no traffic-control signals.

question: A good driver should:
options: a:Focus only on the center of the road.,b:Stare only straight ahead.,c:Watch beside
note: Safe drivers monitor the environment around their vehicle—front, sides, and rear—to anticipate hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what condition may you continue carefully through an intersection with a yellow light?
options: a:If the light turns red as you approach the intersection.,b:If a steady yellow light appears while you are already in the intersection,c:If an emergency vehicle is approaching from behind.,d:If pedestrians are crossing in front of you.
note: If the yellow appears when you are already in the intersection, clear it carefully; otherwise prepare to stop before entering.

question: Is it lawful to drive at night using only your parking lights?
options: a:False,b:True
note: It is unlawful to drive at night using only parking lights; headlights must be used between sunset and sunrise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Only where signs and pavement markings permit passing and you have enough space to do so safely.,b:Within intersections when no oncoming vehicles are visible.,c:On curves if you can see far ahead.,d:In all lanes of a multilane highway at any time.
note: Never pass in intersections or where your view is blocked; pass only where signs and markings permit and it's safe.

question: If weather or lighting conditions require lights, which should you use?
options: a:Only parking lights.,b:Your low-beam headlights.,c:Your high-beam headlights.
note: Use low beams in fog, rain, snow, or other reduced-visibility conditions; high beams can reflect back and worsen visibility.

question: In a vehicle with airbags, where should children age 12 and under ride?
options: a:On an adult's lap in the front seat.,b:In the front seat.,c:In the bed of a pickup truck.,d:In the back seat.
note: Airbags can be dangerous for children; those 12 and under should ride in the back seat.

question: Before driving, you should remove snow, frost, and ice from which parts of your vehicle?
options: a:Only the windshield,b:Only the windshield and passenger window,c:All windows and mirrors
note: You must clear all snow, ice, and frost from ALL vehicle windows and mirrors so you have full visibility before driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, what should you do to check for traffic in your blind spot?
options: a:Rely on the rearview mirror.,b:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,c:Rely on the left side mirror.
note: Glance over your shoulder to check blind spots before changing lanes, in addition to signaling and checking mirrors.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Stop and wait for a green light.,b:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light warns drivers to slow down and cross the intersection carefully, yielding as necessary.

question: Which combination provides the most effective protection in a crash?
options: a:An airbag alone.,b:Only a lap belt.,c:Both a properly worn lap-and-shoulder belt and a correctly functioning airbag.
note: A lap-and-shoulder belt combined with an airbag provides the best protection in a frontal crash; belts should always be worn properly.

question: You check your blind spots by:
options: a:Using the rearview mirror alone.,b:Only using side mirrors exclusively.,c:Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.
note: Blind spots are not visible in mirrors; glance over your shoulder to check them before changing lanes.

question: If another driver cuts you off, what is the safest reaction?
options: a:Flash your high beams at them.,b:Let it go and continue driving safely.,c:Pull next to them and confront them.
note: To avoid road rage and dangerous reactions, let the incident go, slow down, and maintain safe driving behavior.

question: What are the colors of warning signs that indicate upcoming hazards?
options: a:Black on yellow background.,b:White on blue background.,c:Black on white background.
note: Warning signs indicating general hazards are yellow with black symbols or lettering; work zone warnings are orange with black.

question: You may pass another vehicle when the dividing line is a ____ line.
options: a:Double solid yellow,b:Broken white,c:Solid yellow
note: Broken (dashed) white lines separate lanes going in the same direction and permit lane changes and passing when safe.

question: How can you best avoid alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Call a taxi only after you feel intoxicated.,b:Say 'No thanks,c:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.
note: The safest choice is to plan ahead not to drive if you will be drinking; impaired judgment after drinking can prevent safe decisions.

question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, you:
options: a:May still turn but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Have no right to turn and must proceed straight.,c:Retain the arrow's exclusive right-of-way.
note: When a green arrow ends and a solid green remains, turning is allowed but you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians first.

question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
options: a:No passing zones.,b:Railroad crossings.,c:School zones.
note: Crossbucks mark railroad crossings and indicate drivers must yield to any approaching trains.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your turn or exit on a freeway, you should:
options: a:Make the turn quickly from your current lane.,b:Stop and back up on the freeway shoulder.,c:Continue driving until you reach the next exit or safe place to turn around.
note: If you miss an exit, do not stop or back up on the freeway; proceed to the next exit or safe location to change direction.

question: When you park facing uphill on a street with a curb, after setting the parking brake you should:
options: a:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,c:Leave the wheels straight.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb if it moves.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A posted speed limit represents what?
options: a:The suggested speed to travel under ideal conditions.,b:The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel under dangerous conditions.,c:The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel under ideal conditions.
note: Speed limits indicate the lawful maximum or minimum under ideal conditions; you must drive slower when conditions make the posted speed unsafe.

question: If you must park where vehicles are not usually parked, what should you ensure?
options: a:That you park five feet from the curb.,b:That your reverse lights are on while parked.,c:That your vehicle is visible to drivers approaching from any direction.
note: Park so your vehicle does not become a hazard: make it visible to other drivers and use hazard flashers if appropriate.

question: When must headlights be used?
options: a:Whenever the driver is tired.,b:Between sunset and sunrise.,c:Only when the temperature drops below freezing.
note: Headlights are required between sunset and sunrise; use low beams when following or approaching other vehicles to avoid glare.

question: A bicyclist who disobeys traffic laws:
options: a:Must always ride on the sidewalk to avoid tickets.,b:Will always be warned but not ticketed.,c:Can be cited just like a motor vehicle driver.,d:Is exempt from traffic laws and cannot be ticketed.
note: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicle drivers and can be ticketed for violations.

question: Stopping distances and crash severity tend to:
options: a:Decrease as a vehicle's speed increases.,b:Increase as vehicle speed increases.,c:Remain unchanged regardless of speed.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distances and the potential severity of collisions; maintain larger following gaps at speed.

question: How close to a fire hydrant may you legally park?
options: a:No closer than 15 feet from the fire hydrant.,b:No closer than 10 feet from the fire hydrant.,c:No closer than five feet from the fire hydrant.
note: State and local rules generally prohibit parking within 10 feet of a fire hydrant to allow emergency access.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate, what should you do on the entrance/acceleration lane?
options: a:Check traffic, accelerate to match the flow of traffic, and merge when safe.,b:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a large gap.,c:Reduce your speed to 25 mph before merging.
note: Use the acceleration lane to get up to the speed of traffic, signal, check for gaps, and merge smoothly when it is safe.

question: What are potential effects of worn or bald tires?
options: a:They improve fuel economy.,b:They make hydroplaning less likely.,c:They can increase your stopping distance and make turning more difficult.
note: Tires with insufficient tread increase stopping distance, reduce traction in turns, and raise the risk of hydroplaning.

question: When driving in extremely thick fog with very poor visibility, the safest action is to:
options: a:Pull off the roadway, stop, and use emergency flashers until visibility improves.,b:Proceed very slowly (under 10 mph) along the road.,c:Turn on high beams to see farther ahead.,d:Drive in the lane closest to the shoulder.
note: If fog limits visibility severely, safely pull off the road, stop with hazards on, and wait until conditions improve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a ''Yield'' sign you must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to crossing or merging traffic that is close enough to be a hazard.,b:Yield only to vehicles approaching from the right.,c:Always stop even if the way is clear.
note: A yield sign requires you to slow or stop if necessary and give the right-of-way to crossing or merging vehicles and pedestrians.

question: If you start feeling tired while driving, you should:
options: a:Drink an energy drink and keep going.,b:Stop and rest or switch drivers.,c:Open a window for fresh air.
note: If you become fatigued, stop and rest or switch drivers to avoid the dangers of drowsy driving.

question: Which road is most likely to be slippery in cold weather after snow or rain?
options: a:A busy residential street.,b:A shaded area of the road.,c:A hilly
note: Shaded portions of roadway freeze earlier and stay icy longer than exposed sections—use caution.

question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:
options: a:Always signal your intention, even if no other traffic is visible.,b:Signal only if another vehicle is present.,c:Only signal when driving at night.,d:Only signal when turning left.
note: Use your turn signals every time you change lanes, turn, or pull away from a curb.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Must honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know to give you room.,b:Stop and proceed only when there are no pedestrians or vehicles approaching.,c:Drive slowly to allow approaching vehicles and pedestrians time to get out of the way.
note: Always stop before entering the roadway from a driveway and yield to any approaching vehicles or pedestrians; do not cross the sidewalk without stopping first.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the left.,b:Turn your wheels to the right.,c:Keep your wheels straight ahead.
note: When parked facing downhill, turn the wheels toward the curb or edge of the road so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if it moves.

question: Why should you allow extra space in front of a large truck?
options: a:So other drivers can merge in front of you.,b:Because trucks take longer to stop than passenger vehicles travelling at the same speed.,c:Becuase trucks always drive slower.,d:To give the truck driver room to change lanes quickly.
note: Large trucks require more distance to stop, so do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down sharply.

question: Using cruise control on snowy or icy roads is:
options: a:Not safe and should be avoided.,b:Allowed if you have reduced your speed.,c:Recommended to maintain constant speed.
note: Do not use cruise control on slippery surfaces; it can cause loss of vehicle control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a flashing yellow traffic signal, what should you do?
options: a:Increase your speed to clear the intersection quickly.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop every time.
note: A flashing yellow signal warns of a hazard; you should slow down and proceed carefully.

question: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights, what should you do?
options: a:Briefly glance toward the right side of the road or edge of the lane.,b:Focus on the centerline until the car passes.,c:Flash your high beams to warn the other driver.
note: When blinded by oncoming headlights, look briefly toward the right edge of the road to keep your vehicle safely positioned until the vehicle passes.

question: A lack of sleep impairs driving ability in a way similar to which of the following?
options: a:The effect that amphetamines have.,b:The effect that anger has.,c:The effect that alcohol has.
note: Fatigue can impair reaction time, judgment, and alertness similar to alcohol; for example, 18 hours awake is similar to a BAC of about 0.05%.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?
options: a:Passing is allowed only on the right.,b:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:Lanes move in the same direction only.,d:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: A broken yellow centerline allows passing to the left when it is safe and there is no oncoming traffic.

question: Which best describes defensive driving?
options: a:Identifying dangerous driving situations and taking action to avoid accidents.,b:Getting ahead of poor drivers to avoid them.,c:Following the vehicle ahead at a close distance.
note: Defensive driving is anticipating hazards and taking actions to prevent collisions, such as giving extra space and communicating with others.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Speed up to get through wet areas quickly.,b:Use parking lights instead of headlights.,c:Drive at reduced speeds on wet roads and maintain proper tire pressure and tread.,d:Drive with cruise control on wet roads.
note: Hydroplaning risk decreases with lower speeds and well-maintained tires with correct pressure and good tread.

question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, you should:
options: a:Keep a steady pace and stay there.,b:Stay in the blind spot until it is convenient to move.,c:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
note: Do not remain in another vehicle's blind spot; adjust your position so the driver can see you in their mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a steady green traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Proceed but yield to any pedestrians or vehicles already in the intersection.,b:Stop if a police officer is nearby.,c:Treat it as a four-way stop.,d:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
note: On green, you may go but must yield to pedestrians and vehicles already occupying the intersection.

question: What color are traffic control devices used in construction and maintenance areas?
options: a:Red.,b:Orange.,c:Yellow.
note: Orange is used for temporary signs, cones, and barriers in work zones; proceed with caution in these areas.

question: When stopping on snow or ice in a vehicle equipped with ABS, what should you do?
options: a:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,b:Pump the brakes.,c:Stay off the brakes and wait for the car to drift to a stop.
note: On slippery surfaces with ABS, apply firm, continuous pressure to the brake pedal; ABS will modulate the braking.

question: To check blind spots when changing lanes, drivers should:
options: a:Rely only on the left outside mirror.,b:Use the horn instead of looking.,c:Only use the inside rearview mirror.,d:Look over the appropriate shoulder (left or right) in addition to mirror checks.
note: Blind spots can't be seen in mirrors; glance over your shoulder to confirm the lane is clear before changing.

question: Is failure to report an accident that caused property damage of $1,000 or more a criminal offense?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Accidents causing more than $1,000 in property damage (or any injuries) must be reported to law enforcement; failure to report can lead to criminal penalties.

question: What do large flashing arrow panels in work zones indicate?
options: a:Drivers may remain in their current lane.,b:Drivers should merge in the direction of the arrow.,c:The arrow points to something to look at.
note: Flashing arrow panels direct drivers to merge away from a closed lane in construction areas; slow and merge safely.

question: With oncoming traffic to your left and parked vehicles to your right, what steering course should you take?
options: a:Steer a middle course between the oncoming vehicles and the parked vehicles.,b:Steer closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.,c:Steer closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.,d:Swerve back and forth to avoid both.
note: When faced with oncoming and parked vehicles, split the difference and steer a middle course to avoid collisions.

question: A flashing yellow traffic light at an intersection means:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop.,c:Stop and wait until it turns green.,d:Yield only to pedestrians.
note: A flashing yellow indicates caution; you should slow and proceed carefully without stopping unless necessary.

question: If there is an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist to your right, you should:
options: a:Pass the bicyclist before the oncoming car arrives.,b:Pull onto the shoulder immediately.,c:Let the oncoming car pass first,d:Drive between them splitting the difference.
note: When multiple hazards exist, handle them one at a time—wait for the oncoming car before passing the bicyclist.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Signaling before turning, changing lanes, or leaving a curb:
options: a:Is necessary only if other traffic is present.,b:Is necessary only during the maneuver,c:Is a good driving habit and is required by law.
note: The law requires signaling in advance of lane changes or turns — in Maine you should signal at least 100 feet before making the maneuver.

question: Under normal conditions, what minimum following distance should you maintain?
options: a:One second.,b:Two seconds.,c:Three seconds.
note: Keep a minimum two-second following distance under normal conditions; increase it when conditions are poor.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway, you should:
options: a:Drive on the truck's right side and wait to pass.,b:Remain farther back than you would behind a passenger car.,c:Stay closer than you would behind a passenger car.
note: Maintain a greater following distance behind large trucks because they have bigger blind spots and require more stopping distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach an intersection with a steady yellow light and have NOT entered the intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on your hazard lights and proceed.,b:Enter the intersection and then stop,c:Speed up to beat the red light.,d:Come to a safe stop before entering the intersection.
note: A steady yellow warns that the light is about to turn red; if you have not entered the intersection, prepare to stop safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic signals are out due to a power outage, drivers should:
options: a:Turn on hazard lights and go through without stopping.,b:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop,c:Park and wait until power is restored.,d:Follow the same rules as for a flashing yellow light.
note: When lights are out, yield as you would at a four-way stop and proceed when it's your turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If driving next to a single broken white line, you may:
options: a:Never cross the line to pass.,b:Only cross to change lanes if you are in the left lane.,c:Cross the line to pass or change lanes when safe.
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to pass or change lanes when safe.

question: If your vehicle develops a mechanical problem while driving, you should:
options: a:Stop in your lane and leave hazard lights off.,b:Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road as soon as safely possible.,c:Signal and move into the slow lane and continue driving.,d:Continue driving at reduced speed until you reach a service area.
note: If possible, get the vehicle off the road, away from traffic, and use emergency flashers to warn other drivers.

question: How are bicycles on the road regarded under traffic laws?
options: a:They must always yield the right-of-way to motor vehicles.,b:They are considered vehicles and have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.,c:They do not follow specific rules of the road.
note: Bicyclists are road users with the same rights and duties as motor vehicle drivers; motorists should respect and share the road.

question: What do two solid yellow lines painted on the pavement signify?
options: a:Passing is allowed if you are at the top of a hill.,b:Passing is not allowed.,c:Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.
note: Two solid yellow lines indicate traffic traveling in opposite directions and prohibit passing from either side.

question: What do your brake lights tell other drivers?
options: a:You have your emergency brake on.,b:You are making a turn.,c:You are slowing down or stopping.
note: Brake lights indicate to following drivers that you are reducing speed or stopping; they must be in working order whenever you drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto the freeway, you should be driving:
options: a:Well below the speed limit.,b:At any slow speed to wait for a gap.,c:At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.
note: Enter the freeway at or near the speed of traffic so you can merge smoothly; if traffic is over the speed limit, do not exceed legal limits.

question: Backing up a vehicle is:
options: a:Always risky and requires extra caution.,b:Safe if no helper is present.,c:Only dangerous in large vehicles.,d:Not dangerous when aided by mirrors alone.
note: Reversing is hazardous due to limited visibility; use caution and helpers when necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must stop at an intersection when you see which signal?
options: a:A flashing green light.,b:A flashing red light.,c:A steady yellow light.,d:A yellow arrow.
note: A flashing red traffic signal requires a full stop before proceeding when the way is clear.

question: If your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement, what is the correct immediate action?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas, steer parallel to the road, slow down, and then ease back onto the pavement when safe.,b:Stop quickly.,c:Accelerate and steer back onto the road quickly.
note: Do not panic; slow gradually, steer parallel to the road, check for traffic, and when safe, ease back onto the pavement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Are you required to signal any time you pull away from a curb?
options: a:Yes — you must signal whenever you pull away from a curb.,b:No — signaling is optional when leaving a curb.,c:Only if another vehicle is present.,d:Only on multi-lane streets.
note: You must use the proper turn signal every time you pull away from a curb to indicate your intentions to other road users.

question: Distracted drivers are at greater risk of a crash when using which device?
options: a:Radio.,b:CD player.,c:Cell phone.
note: Using a cell phone (even hands-free) is a major distraction and increases crash risk.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check a blind spot?
options: a:Never,b:Only when pulling to or from a curb.,c:When changing lanes.
note: Always glance over your shoulder to check blind spots before changing lanes, turning, or moving laterally.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is required for safe interstate driving?
options: a:No special skills beyond local driving.,b:Only the ability to drive fast,c:Both the ability to safely drive at increased speeds and constant alertness.,d:Only constant alertness while driving slowly.
note: Interstate driving demands both the capacity to safely travel at higher speeds and continuous alertness to traffic conditions.

question: Many crashes are caused by:
options: a:Drivers yielding the right-of-way.,b:Drivers going too fast for conditions.,c:Drivers frequently checking mirrors and blind spots.
note: Excessive speed for conditions is a common cause of crashes; adjust speed to road and weather conditions.

question: When must you obey instructions from a school crossing guard?
options: a:Only during school hours.,b:Only if you see children present.,c:At all times.
note: Drivers must obey crossing guards' instructions at all times when they are performing crossing duties near schools or crosswalks.

question: What is the meaning of a diamond-shaped traffic sign?
options: a:Regulatory — you must follow it.,b:Warning — special conditions or hazards ahead.,c:Stop required ahead.,d:Information — services ahead.
note: Diamond-shaped signs, usually yellow or orange, warn drivers of special conditions or hazards on or near the road.

question: Continuous hard braking on ice and snow often:
options: a:Helps you stop faster.,b:Prevents the brakes from freezing.,c:Locks the front wheels and causes loss of steering.
note: Hard, continuous braking can lock wheels on slippery surfaces and cause loss of steering control; slow and brake gently.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are being passed on both sides while driving in the center lane of an expressway, what should you do?
options: a:Move to the left lane regardless of traffic.,b:Remain in the center lane and maintain speed.,c:Speed up to prevent others from passing.,d:Move to the lane on your right if it is safe to do so.
note: On multi-lane highways, drive in the right lanes unless you are passing or turning left; move right if you are being passed on both sides.

question: Large trucks are likely to lose speed under which condition?
options: a:When driving down long,b:When driving in long,c:When driving up long or steep hills.
note: Because trucks are heavy, they may slow significantly when climbing long or steep grades; give them extra space.

question: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, when may vehicles behind the bus proceed?
options: a:When all students are off the bus.,b:When the children wave to you.,c:When the stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.
note: Motorists must remain stopped until the bus turns off its red lights, retracts the stop arm, and begins moving again.

question: A double yellow centerline painted down the road means passing is:
options: a:Not allowed from either direction.,b:Allowed only from your direction of travel.,c:Allowed from both directions.
note: Double yellow centerlines separate opposing traffic and indicate no passing by vehicles traveling in either direction.

question: Which color lines separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Red,b:White,c:Black
note: Yellow lines separate opposing traffic; white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. (Note: the correct answer color is yellow.)

question: A leaking exhaust system can cause you to become:
options: a:To use more oil.,b:Drowsy while driving.,c:To need a tune-up sooner.
note: Exhaust leaks can allow carbon monoxide into the vehicle, causing drowsiness, unconsciousness, or worse.

question: What can happen if you take a prescription drug and also drink alcohol?
options: a:It can make you unfit to drive and increase impairment.,b:It will make you more alert.,c:There will likely be no effect.
note: Combining alcohol with prescription or over-the-counter medications can increase drowsiness, slow reactions, and make you unsafe to drive.

question: Which of the following will help someone sober up after drinking alcohol?
options: a:Drinking coffee and getting fresh air.,b:Nothing but the passage of time will reduce impairment.,c:Taking a cold shower and drinking tomato juice.
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize alcohol; coffee, fresh air, or other remedies do not sober a person.

question: When making a turn, what should you do with your speed?
options: a:Reduce your speed to maintain control of the vehicle.,b:Increase your speed to make a quicker turn.,c:Maintain highway speed.,d:Come to a complete stop every time before turning.
note: Slow to a safe speed that allows you to stay in your lane and maintain control during the turn.

question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, the best course of action is to:
options: a:Turn up the radio volume to stay alert.,b:Stop driving and rest.,c:Drink coffee and continue driving.,d:Open a window and keep driving.
note: Fatigue impairs driving similarly to alcohol; stopping to rest is the safest choice.

question: Must drivers stop when a school bus is using its flashing red lights?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Stop when a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended; on divided highways with a median, opposite-direction traffic may not have to stop.

question: On a multilane road, a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means what?
options: a:Passing is prohibited from both directions.,b:Passing is permitted from both directions.,c:Passing is permitted only from the direction next to the dashed line.
note: Where solid and dashed yellow lines are paired, only traffic adjacent to the dashed line may cross to pass.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway, how should your following distance compare to that behind a passenger vehicle?
options: a:No more than one car length behind the truck.,b:Closely behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead.,c:Farther behind the truck than you would when following a passenger vehicle.
note: Trucks need more stopping distance and have large blind spots; maintain a greater following distance so you remain visible to the truck driver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection, what should a driver do?
options: a:Yield to all other drivers no matter the situation.,b:Stop and check in all directions,c:Maintain their speed and proceed without checking.
note: At intersections without signs or signals, slow, check left and right, yield to vehicles from the right if necessary, and proceed when safe.

question: How does increasing your vehicle's speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:It decreases your field of vision as speed increases.,b:It increases your field of vision.,c:It makes it easier to see cross traffic.,d:It has no effect.
note: The faster you drive, the smaller your effective field of vision becomes, so increased speed requires greater alertness.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: With a solid yellow line on one side and a broken yellow on your side, when may you pass?
options: a:Only on expressways.,b:You may pass if the way ahead is clear.,c:Only in an emergency.
note: If the broken yellow line is next to your lane, you may cross it to pass when it is safe and there is no oncoming traffic.

question: Before changing lanes, what is the correct sequence of checks and signals?
options: a:Begin signaling as you move into the lane.,b:Signal at least 500 feet before your lane change in residential areas.,c:Check mirrors
note: Always check mirrors, look over your shoulder to view blind spots, then signal well before you change lanes.

question: Which statement about passing motorcycles is true?
options: a:Motorcycles with two riders are always more stable than with one.,b:You must move completely into the adjacent lane when passing a motorcycle.,c:You can pass a motorcycle without changing lanes.,d:Other vehicles may follow motorcycles closely.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane; when passing, change lanes completely to provide safe space.

question: Where is it appropriate to use high beam headlights?
options: a:Where pedestrians may be present and no other vehicles are near.,b:Only on familiar roads.,c:In construction areas where no nearby vehicles are present.
note: Use high beams when there are no nearby vehicles to improve visibility—on unfamiliar roads, in construction areas, or where people may be along the roadside—then dim for other vehicles.

question: Is it ever acceptable to drive around or under a moving railroad crossing gate?
options: a:Only if your vehicle can clear it without damage.,b:If you look both ways first and see no trains.,c:No—never drive around or under a lowering or lowered gate.
note: Do not go around or under crossing gates; wait until lights stop flashing, bells stop, and gates are fully raised.

question: If a child appears likely to run into the street in front of your vehicle, what should you do immediately?
options: a:Flash your headlights.,b:Sound a sharp blast of your horn.,c:Start to prepare to slow down.
note: If someone, especially a child, is about to enter the street in front of you, use a sharp horn blast to warn them and apply the brakes as needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these statements about changing lanes is correct?
options: a:Vehicles with two outside mirrors do not have blind spots.,b:Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.,c:You only need to turn and look over your right shoulder for lane changes to the right or left.
note: Before changing lanes signal, check mirrors, and look over the shoulder toward the lane you intend to enter to verify the blind spot is clear.

question: Large vehicles generally have:
options: a:Smaller blind spots due to higher seating.,b:No blind spots at all.,c:Larger blind spots than smaller vehicles.
note: Bigger vehicles like trucks and buses have larger blind spots, especially close to their rear and sides.

question: Use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days for what reason?
options: a:To keep your engine warm.,b:To warn others of bad weather conditions.,c:So others can see your vehicle.
note: If weather conditions reduce visibility, turning on your low beam headlights makes your vehicle easier for others to see; in Maine, if wipers are required, headlights must be on.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To change lanes safely, what sequence should you use?
options: a:Signal,b:Use turn indicator,c:Check mirrors and signal
note: Before changing lanes, signal, check rearview and side mirrors, glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot, and then move when safe.

question: Are drivers always required to stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road?
options: a:,b:FALSE,c:TRUE
note: Drivers on both directions of a two-lane road must stop for a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended and lights flashing.

question: What does an ''End school zone'' sign indicate?
options: a:The beginning of a reduced speed zone.,b:The speed limit is 20 mph at all times.,c:The end of a reduced school speed zone.
note: An 'End school zone' sign marks the end of the reduced school speed zone; observe posted speed limits outside the zone.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a railroad crossing without electric warning devices, you should:
options: a:Drive through without stopping if no train is visible.,b:Slow,c:Speed up and cross quickly.
note: If a crossing lacks active warnings, reduce speed, look both ways, and listen for approaching trains before crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver's left arm extended upward indicates they plan to:
options: a:Stop.,b:Turn left.,c:Turn right.
note: Left arm up is the hand signal for a right turn; be aware when following such a vehicle.

question: Before backing out of your driveway and with children nearby you should:
options: a:Rev your engine to warn them.,b:Walk to the rear of your vehicle to ensure the way is clear.,c:Sound your horn only.
note: When children are nearby, exit the vehicle and check behind it rather than relying solely on mirrors or horns.

question: What do double solid yellow lane markings indicate?
options: a:Both lanes may pass.,b:Neither lane may pass.,c:The lane to the right may pass.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and prohibit passing for vehicles in both directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive faster than:
options: a:The posted maximum speed limit only.,b:What feels comfortable for you.,c:What is reasonable and prudent given conditions
note: You must drive at a speed that is reasonable and prudent for the conditions (road, weather, traffic, visibility) and within legal limits.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:
options: a:Assume the guard shouldn't be directing traffic.,b:Copy what other drivers do even if it contradicts the guard.,c:Follow the crossing guard's directions.
note: Follow directions from crossing guards and law enforcement in school zones and exercise extra caution.

question: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line indicates:
options: a:Passing is not allowed in either direction.,b:Both directions may pass.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line but not from the lane next to the solid line.
note: If your side has the broken line, you may pass when safe; if your side has the solid line, you may not.

question: Which statement best completes the sentence: ''____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory''?
options: a:Alcohol does not,b:Even the smallest amount of alcohol can,c:Only a blood alcohol level greater than the legal limit can
note: Even small amounts of alcohol impair concentration, perception, judgment, and memory; no amount is safe for driving.

question: A person using a white cane or a guide dog is most likely to be:
options: a:A person involved in a traffic study.,b:A deaf person.,c:A blind or visually impaired person.
note: Drivers must always yield the right-of-way to pedestrians who are blind or visually impaired and who use a white cane or guide dog.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a stop sign, what sequence should you use to check for cross traffic before entering the intersection?
options: a:Move when the vehicle ahead moves regardless of cross traffic.,b:Look right first,c:Check your rearview mirror for tailgaters only.
note: When stopped, look right first because vehicles from that side are closest, then left, then right again to ensure a clear path.

question: What should you do before driving if you are taking any medicine?
options: a:Consult your doctor or pharmacist about how it may affect your driving.,b:Have someone follow you home, even if medication is fine.,c:Open your windows and drive slower.,d:Double the dose to speed up recovery.
note: Both prescription and over-the-counter medicines can impair driving; always check with your doctor or pharmacist.

question: When changing lanes, you should look for a gap of about:
options: a:Four seconds,b:One to two seconds,c:Three seconds
note: A four-second gap gives you enough space to merge safely and maintain adequate following distance.

question: To safely pass a bicyclist you should:
options: a:Drive in the bicycle lane until you complete the pass.,b:Honk to signal your intention.,c:Slow down and give the bicyclist as much space as possible.
note: Give bicyclists ample room when passing and slow down to avoid startling or crowding them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes on a highway, which of the following actions should you perform?
options: a:Signal a lane change only.,b:Check your rearview and outside mirrors only.,c:Check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder.
note: When changing lanes you should signal, check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots before moving into the new lane.

question: Alcohol in any concentration is classified as:
options: a:A stimulant.,b:A depressant.,c:Neither of the above.
note: Alcohol is a central nervous system depressant that slows reactions, impairs judgment, and reduces coordination.

question: When approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, what should you do?
options: a:Stop,b:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.,c:Yield to all traffic before crossing the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down to a safe speed and proceed with caution through the intersection.

question: If a large vehicle is overtaking you, you should:
options: a:Maintain your speed or slow down slightly.,b:Speed up to prevent it from passing.,c:Immediately move into the left lane without signaling.
note: Do not increase speed when being passed by a large vehicle; maintain speed or slow down a bit to let it pass safely.

question: At a red light with a green arrow, you may proceed in the arrow's direction if:
options: a:You first come to a complete stop.,b:You wait until the light changes to solid green.,c:You are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear.
note: A green arrow allows movement in its direction while the arrow is displayed, but you must ensure the path is clear before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do at an intersection with a flashing red light?
options: a:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,b:Stop only if other cars are approaching.,c:Come to a full stop
note: A flashing red light functions like a stop sign: stop, yield, then continue when the way is clear.

question: Distracted driving typically:
options: a:Is never dangerous.,b:Helps drivers respond faster.,c:Causes slower reactions to hazards.
note: Any distraction usually slows reaction times and reduces the driver's ability to respond to hazards.

question: As you near the top of a hill, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Maintain a steady speed.,b:Speed up slightly.,c:Prepare to stop if necessary.
note: You may not see hazards over the crest, so reduce speed as needed and be ready to stop for stalled vehicles or other obstructions.

question: A sign reading “Reduced speed, 35 mph” means:
options: a:The previous speed limit still applies until the next sign.,b:You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced zone.,c:The reduced 35 mph speed limit begins at that sign.,d:The reduced speed begins at the next sign.
note: A 'Reduced speed' sign sets the new speed limit at the location of the sign.

question: Alcohol affects your driving by:
options: a:Improving driving skills while harming judgment.,b:Harming both driving skills and judgment.,c:Having no effect on either.
note: Alcohol impairs reaction time, coordination, vision, and judgment, increasing crash risk.

question: Which headlight setting should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:No lights at all.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.,d:High beam headlights.
note: Use low beams in fog, rain, or snow because high beams create glare and reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two drivers reach a four-way stop at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the right.,b:Either driver may proceed without stopping.,c:The driver on the left.
note: If two vehicles arrive simultaneously at a four-way stop, yield to the vehicle on your right; proceed when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a steady yellow traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Ignore it because they have right-of-way.,b:Speed up to clear the intersection.,c:Slow to a stop unless already in the intersection.
note: A steady yellow warns that the light will soon be red; stop unless you are already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, what checks should you perform first?
options: a:Honk your horn at least three times.,b:Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.,c:Check your mirrors and blind spots.
note: Before passing, check mirrors, glance over your shoulder for blind spots, and signal before changing lanes; re-enter when it is safe.

question: Airbags provide complete protection in a crash. Is this true or false?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Airbags provide added protection in frontal impacts but do not replace safety belts; you must wear a seat belt to get full protection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a two-lane road, what must you judge before pulling out?
options: a:Flash your headlights as you pass.,b:Sound your horn as you pass.,c:Judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles.
note: On two-lane roads you must be sure you have enough room and time to pass safely by assessing the distance and speed of any oncoming traffic.

question: Which of the following is a dangerous habit in work zones?
options: a:Tailgating another vehicle.,b:Failing to carefully watch for workers and moving equipment.,c:Both of the above.
note: In work zones, do not follow too closely and be alert for workers and machinery; both tailgating and inattention increase crash risk.

question: Tailgating (following too closely) can:
options: a:Reduce collisions by preventing others from cutting in.,b:Improve traffic flow in congested areas.,c:Never result in a traffic citation.,d:Provoke and frustrate other drivers and can lead to citations.
note: Following too closely is dangerous, can cause aggressive driving incidents, and may be illegal.

question: What does an arrow painted in a traffic lane on the pavement require drivers to do?
options: a:Drivers must come to a complete stop before following the arrow.,b:Drivers in that lane may choose to ignore the arrow.,c:The arrow applies only when traffic signals are not functioning.,d:Drivers in that lane must make the movement indicated by the arrow.
note: An arrow painted within a traffic lane tells drivers in that lane they must make the movement shown, subject to any traffic signs or signals.

question: If a vehicle has airbags, what about seat belts?
options: a:Seat belts should still be worn.,b:Seat belts are unnecessary.,c:Seat belts only needed in the back seats.
note: Airbags supplement but do not replace seat belts; always wear lap and shoulder belts for full protection.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, what must other drivers allow for?
options: a:The decreased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,b:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,c:The decreased noise of larger vehicles.
note: Large trucks require longer stopping distances; smaller vehicle drivers should position themselves where they can be seen and where their view is not blocked.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic signal require of a driver?
options: a:Come to a complete stop at the intersection.,b:Maintain your normal speed.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution; slow down and be alert for cross traffic or hazards.

question: Should you use high beams when driving in fog?
options: a:Use parking lights only.,b:Yes — high beams improve visibility.,c:Alternate high and low beams frequently.,d:No — use low beams in fog.
note: High beams reflect off fog and reduce visibility; low beams are the correct choice when driving in fog.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with only a crossbuck, what should you do?
options: a:Only continue once cleared by a flagger.,b:Turn your radio down to hear an approaching train.,c:Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
note: Approach all railroad crossings cautiously and only proceed when there is no train coming from either direction; follow any flagger instructions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a left-turn lane to turn, what should you do as you approach the intersection with oncoming traffic?
options: a:Turn your front wheels to the left to be prepared to turn.,b:Signal about 100 feet before the turn and keep your front wheels straight until you begin the turn.,c:Move to the left of the center lane.
note: Signal ahead of time and keep your wheels straight so you will not be pushed into oncoming traffic if struck from behind.

question: If you see other drivers acting angrily, you should:
options: a:Put distance between yourself and them and avoid engaging.,b:Make eye contact to calm them down.,c:Respond with hand gestures.,d:Drive faster to get away immediately.
note: Physically and mentally distance yourself from angry drivers to reduce risk of conflict.

question: What should you remember when driving on wet pavement?
options: a:Wet roads always improve traction.,b:You can stop in the same distance as on dry roads.,c:Roads can be especially slippery right after rain begins.
note: Wet roads are most slippery when rain first mixes with oils on the pavement. Slow down, increase following distance, and be cautious of hydroplaning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are required to stop your vehicle when:
options: a:All of the above,b:Facing a red traffic signal.,c:Approaching an intersection with a stop sign.,d:Where a traffic officer orders you to stop.
note: You must stop at stop signs, at red lights, and whenever directed to stop by a traffic officer.

question: What is the only effective way to reduce your BAC?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Exercise.,c:Allow your body time to eliminate the alcohol.
note: Only time allows your body to metabolize and lower blood alcohol concentration; other measures do not reduce BAC.

question: Drivers must keep a safe distance when near a cyclist.
options: a:False,b:True
note: Drivers should always maintain a safe operating distance from bicyclists and be especially careful when passing or sharing the road.

question: In very heavy fog you should slow down and:
options: a:Turn on your low beam headlights.,b:Turn on high beams to see further.,c:Turn on emergency flashers only.
note: Use low beams or fog lights in dense fog; high beams reflect and worsen visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching a railroad crossing warning sign you should:
options: a:Look for ways around any lowered gates.,b:Try to drive faster than the train to clear the tracks.,c:Be prepared to stop if a train is near.
note: Warning signs indicate a possible train; be prepared to stop and always obey crossing devices.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down,b:Stop on the edge of the road immediately.,c:Brake hard and sharply steer back onto the pavement.
note: If your wheels drop onto a low shoulder, reduce speed without heavy braking, check traffic, then gently steer back onto the pavement.

question: Collisions are most likely to occur when:
options: a:All vehicles travel at about the same speed.,b:One vehicle is traveling significantly faster or slower than the flow of traffic.,c:One lane of traffic is traveling faster than other lanes.
note: Crashes often occur when a vehicle's speed is inconsistent with the surrounding traffic; matching the flow within the speed limit reduces risk.

question: What does a pentagon-shaped sign indicate?
options: a:School zone or school crossing.,b:Stop sign.,c:Regulatory sign.
note: A five-sided (pentagon) sign usually alerts drivers to a school zone or school crossing where children may be present.

question: Where should your hands be placed on the steering wheel when driving normally?
options: a:At the 1 and 11 o'clock positions.,b:One hand at the top of the wheel.,c:At the 2 and 10 o'clock positions on the wheel.,d:At the 3 and 9 o'clock positions.
note: To maintain control while driving normally, place your hands on the outside of the wheel at the 2 and 10 o'clock positions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A U-turn is prohibited:
options: a:On a straight road with a clear 500-foot view.,b:On or near any curve or hill.,c:In a parking lot.
note: Never perform a U-turn on or near a curve or hill where oncoming traffic may not be visible; it creates a collision hazard.

question: Alcohol affects drivers by:
options: a:Slowing reaction time, impairing thinking, and giving false confidence.,b:Speeding reaction time up safely.,c:Improving coordination and vision.,d:Having no effect if you feel sober.
note: Alcohol reduces reaction speed, judgment, and coordination and can create false confidence.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct method for making a right turn?
options: a:Approach in the right lane but move toward the middle of the street before turning.,b:Signal,c:Use turn indicator
note: Before turning right, signal, slow, and position your vehicle as close as practical to the right curb or edge of the roadway.

question: Having a driver license is considered a:
options: a:Right.,b:Requirement.,c:Privilege.
note: Driving is a privilege granted by the state and may be suspended or revoked for violations.

question: If you see or hear an approaching emergency vehicle while driving on a divided multilane highway, you should:
options: a:Stop as quickly as possible in your lane.,b:Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.,c:Slow
note: Provide a clear path—slow down, move aside safely, and stop if necessary so the emergency vehicle can pass.

question: In which situations is it important to slow down?
options: a:At intersections or railroad crossings.,b:All of the above.,c:On narrow or winding roads.,d:When the road is wet or slippery.
note: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections and railroad crossings, on hills, and whenever road conditions are poor or visibility is reduced.

question: Which of the following about blind spots is true?
options: a:They can be checked only with rearview mirrors.,b:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,c:They are removed if you have one outside mirror on each side.
note: Mirrors don't eliminate blind spots; large trucks have especially large no-zones that other drivers should avoid.

question: When are roads most likely to be very slippery after rain begins?
options: a:The day after it rains.,b:For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.,c:After it has been raining steadily for several hours.
note: Road surfaces can become especially slippery during the first 10–15 minutes of rainfall as oils on the pavement rise to the surface.

question: Which of the following helps you drive more safely at night?
options: a:Drive only with parking lights on.,b:Ignore headlights and keep using high beams.,c:Increase your following distance to allow more reaction time.,d:Depend on interior lights to see controls.
note: At night, reduce speed, increase following distance, and ensure headlights are working properly to improve safety.

question: If someone is injured in an accident, what should you do?
options: a:Not move the injured unless necessary; keep them warm and provide first aid if qualified.,b:Move the injured immediately away from the scene at all costs.,c:Leave the injured where they are and drive to get help.
note: Do not move injured persons unnecessarily; movement can worsen injuries. Keep them warm, render first aid if trained, and wait for medical personnel.

question: To reduce headlight glare from oncoming vehicles at night, where should you direct your gaze?
options: a:Straight ahead.,b:Over your shoulder.,c:Toward the right side of the road ahead.
note: If oncoming headlights blind you, look to the right side of the roadway ahead to reduce glare while staying aware of the lane limits.

question: Which statement about drugs and driving is true?
options: a:Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.,b:Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.,c:Any prescription is safe to use while driving.
note: Both prescription and over-the-counter medications can impair driving; it is unlawful to drive while impaired by any drug.

question: A red flashing traffic light has the same meaning as a:
options: a:Stop sign.,b:Solid red light.,c:Yield sign.
note: A red flashing traffic light means stop, just like a stop sign. Proceed only when it is safe.

question: What is the best way to avoid dangerous situations while driving?
options: a:Turn off the radio and avoid scanning mirrors.,b:Always keep your eyes focused only straight ahead.,c:Constantly be aware of what is happening around your vehicle.
note: Use continuous observation—front, sides, and rear—so you can anticipate hazards and adjust speed or position as needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From top to bottom, what is the proper order of lights on a vertical traffic signal?
options: a:Red,b:You red,c:Green
note: On vertical traffic signals red is always on top, yellow in the middle, and green on the bottom.

question: On a dimly lit street at night, you should:
options: a:Use high beams to better see the road ahead.,b:Keep instrument panel lights very bright so others see you.,c:Drive slowly enough to stop within the area lit by your headlights.
note: Reduce speed at night so you can stop within the distance illuminated by your headlights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.,b:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:When you are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: Do not return to the driving lane until you can clearly see the passed vehicle's front headlights in your rearview mirror.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you check for traffic when entering a freeway?
options: a:Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder in the direction of the merge.,b:Only use your rearview mirror.,c:Use your rearview and side mirrors without turning your head.
note: When merging onto a freeway, use mirrors and a quick shoulder check to detect vehicles in your blind spot and choose a safe gap.

question: In fog, you should use:
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Four-way flashers primarily.
note: Low beams improve visibility in fog; high beams reflect and worsen visibility.

question: When traveling to an unfamiliar area, what should you do before you leave?
options: a:Start with a general idea and figure it out while driving.,b:Depend only on road signs to find your way.,c:Plan your route in advance.
note: Plan your trip ahead of time and check maps or directions so you do not rely solely on unfamiliar road signs while driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or False: Drivers may pass on a two-lane road when there is a single solid yellow line on their side of the centerline.
options: a:True,b:False
note: A solid yellow line on your side means passing is prohibited. Passing is allowed only when the broken line is on your side.

question: When passing a bicyclist on a two-lane road without bike lanes, the safest method is to:
options: a:Slow down, wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass leaving sufficient space.,b:Pass quickly and close to the cyclist to minimize lane time.,c:Never pass until a traffic signal or stop sign.
note: Give cyclists at least 3 feet (more at higher speeds) and only pass when it's safe with no oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches while you're on a one-way street, you must:
options: a:Turn on your hazard flashers and keep moving.,b:Keep driving until you reach the next block.,c:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.
